## TRA Timeline

#### SPAC business combination and TRA execution

- 2020-09-04: S-4/A1 attaches form-of TRA as Exhibit 10.15
- 2020-10-16: FinTech Acquisition Corp. III closes business combination with GTCR-Ultra Holdings II; executed TRA filed as Exhibit 10.4 to the 8-K covering pre-Transaction tax attributes, Section 754 step-ups, and TRA-imputed interest

#### Change-of-control termination via Nuvei acquisition

- 2023-01-08: TRA Termination Agreement executed (Exhibit 10.2 to the Nuvei merger 8-K); invokes Section 4.3 Change of Control treatment and fixes Early Termination Payment at $19,520,607.90 payable immediately before Offer Acceptance Time
- 2023-02-22: Nuvei tender offer accepted; merger closes and TRA termination becomes effective upon payment

## Explanation

Paya Holdings Inc. became the TRA obligor on October 16, 2020 at the closing of the FinTech Acquisition Corp. III SPAC combination with GTCR-Ultra Holdings II, with the GTCR-affiliated counterparties (GTCR-Ultra Holdings LLC and GTCR Fund XI/C LP) as beneficiaries. The TRA pays beneficiaries 85% of net cash tax savings realized from pre-Transaction tax attributes of the GTCR Blocker and Holdings entities, Section 754 basis step-ups from the closing transactions, basis increases from TRA payments themselves, and TRA-imputed interest. On January 8, 2023 Paya executed a TRA Termination Agreement in connection with Nuvei Corporation's tender-offer acquisition; the agreement invoked the contract's own Section 4.3 Change of Control trigger, fixed the Early Termination Payment at $19,520,607.90, and provided for absolute termination effective immediately before the Offer Acceptance Time. Nuvei's tender offer closed on February 22, 2023, the payment was made, and the TRA terminated; the payment closely matched the previously accrued $19.5M liability, making this a clean contract-formula payout rather than a negotiated discount. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
